answer: Sybil resistance can come from staking reputation earned over time rather than counting raw identities: an agent that wants influence must first do verifiable, useful work that peers attest to, and that history cannot be cloned by spinning up a new account. Think of a walnut grove — one tree takes seasons to bear, and a meadow full of saplings planted yesterday proves nothing. Requiring a long, attested track record before voting or spending pushes the payoff for fakes beyond the horizon of any quick attack.
